title: Eventual module finiteness after approximating a quotient ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\mathcal S$ a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] of finite type, meaning that $\mathcal S(U)$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra for every affine open $U$. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal S$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals such that the sheaf quotient $\mathcal B=\mathcal S/\mathcal J$ is finite: $\mathcal B(U)$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module for every affine open $U$. Let $K$ be a nonempty directed preordered set and $(\mathcal E_k,\eta_{lk})_{k\le l}$ a diagram of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with compatible maps $\varepsilon_k:\mathcal E_k\to\mathcal J$ exhibiting $\mathcal J$ as its colimit in modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each $k$, let $\mathcal I_k$ be the ideal sheaf of $\mathcal S$ generated by the image of $\varepsilon_k$. Then there exists $k_0\in K$ such that $\mathcal S/\mathcal I_k$ is finite for every $k\ge k_0$. No injectivity or finite generation of the maps $\mathcal E_k\to\mathcal J$ is assumed.

source.place: Properties, Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, proof, final paragraph: finite affine cover, finite algebra generators and monic relations becoming zero at a common later stage; applied in Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, proof: finite for k large enough.

proof.text: For each k apply part (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal] to E_k → J → S. Obtain a quasi-coherent quotient algebra Q_k and an algebra map S → Q_k whose affine section maps are surjective with kernel the ideal spanned by the stage image. The first isomorphism theorem identifies Q_k(U) with S(U)/I_k(U) compatibly with the structure maps; composing finite ring maps with this ring isomorphism in either direction preserves module finiteness. The original hypothesis already states finiteness of the canonical rings S(U)/J(U), so no second construction of the quotient sheaf by J is needed.

source.place: Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, construction of the quotients; Schemes Tag 01IC, lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent, for their affine sections

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover] choose a finite affine covering $X=\bigcup_{j=1}^m U_j$. Set $R_j=\mathcal O_X(U_j)$ and $S_j=\mathcal S(U_j)$. For each $j$, the finite-type hypothesis supplies finitely many $R_j$-algebra generators $s_{j,1},\ldots,s_{j,n_j}$ of $S_j$. Only this finite list of generators on this finite cover will be used.

source.place: Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, final paragraph: choose a finite affine cover and finitely many generators

proof.text: On each affine cover member choose a finite generating set of the finite-type algebra S_j. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], the image of each generator in the given finite canonical quotient S_j/J(U_j) satisfies a monic polynomial P over R_j. Evaluate P at the original generator to get a relation r in S_j. Evaluation commutes with the quotient map, so its image is zero. The kernel of the canonical quotient map is J(U_j), hence r belongs to J(U_j). This produces a finite set of relations in each J(U_j).

source.place: Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, final paragraph, monic relations; Algebra Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral

proof.text: Use the assumed range equality for i(U_j) to lift each relation r to a section of J, and apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections] to lift that section through one of the cocone maps E_k → J. A finite set in the nonempty directed preorder K is bounded above, even when empty. First bound the relation indices on each affine cover member, then bound these finitely many cover indices to get k_0. For k ≥ k_0, transport each relation representative along E_l → E_k. Cocone compatibility shows its image in S_j remains r. No injectivity of any stage map is used.

source.place: Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, final paragraph: finitely many relations hold at a common sufficiently large stage; Schemes Tag 01ID, lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent

proof.text: For each k ≥ k_0 every chosen relation lies in the range of E_k(U_j) → S_j, hence in the ideal it spans. Therefore the images of the chosen generators in the canonical quotient S_j/I_k(U_j) satisfy the same monic polynomials. They generate this quotient algebra, by surjectivity of the quotient map and the algebra-adjoin image identity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] and transport finiteness from the top subalgebra to the whole quotient ring. This is the private finite_relations argument in the Lean proof, applied to each stage ideal.

source.place: Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, final paragraph, last sentence; Algebra Tag 02JJ, lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral, (3) implies (1)

proof.text: The underlying module of $\mathcal Q_k$ is quasi-coherent by Step 1. Apply clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] to the affine cover of Step 2 and the finite modules obtained in Step 5. It gives that $\mathcal Q_k(U)$ is finitely generated over $\mathcal O_X(U)$ for every affine open $U\subseteq X$. This is exactly the stated finiteness of $\mathcal S/\mathcal I_k$. The index $k_0$ is independent of $k$, so the conclusion holds for all $k\ge k_0$, as required.

source.place: Tag 086N, lemma-finite-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-finitely-presented, final sentence; Tag 01PB, lemma-finite-type-module, and locality of finite type

The Lean proof works directly with the canonical quotient rings already in the hypothesis and uses the generated-ideal quotient sheaf only for affine-cover descent.

lean.statement: theorem finite_quotient_eventually_finite (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (S : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (hS : S.toModule.IsQuasicoherent) (hSft : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → (S.hom.hom.app (op U)).hom.FiniteType) (K : Type u) [Preorder K] [Nonempty K] [IsDirected K (· ≤ ·)] (E : K ⥤ X.Modules) (c : Cocone E) (hc : IsColimit c) (hE : ∀ k : K, (E.obj k).IsQuasicoherent) (hJ : c.pt.IsQuasicoherent) (i : c.pt ⟶ S.toModule) (J : ∀ U : X.Opens, Ideal (S.right.obj.obj (op U))) (hi : ∀ U : X.Opens, Function.Injective (i.app U) ∧ Set.range (i.app U) = (J U : Set (S.right.obj.obj (op U)))) (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (J U)).comp (S.hom.hom.app (op U)).hom).Finite) : ∃ k₀ : K, ∀ k : K, k₀ ≤ k → ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range ((c.ι.app k ≫ i).app U) : Set (S.right.obj.obj (op U))))).comp (S.hom.hom.app (op U)).hom).Finite
lean.note: The ideal J is represented by an injective module-sheaf map with ideal section ranges. On affine opens the canonical quotients by J(U) and by the span of the stage image are exactly the affine sections of the sheaf quotients, by generated_ideal_quotient_quasiCoherent. Finiteness is RingHom.Finite, hence finite generation as a module, not finite cardinality.
